decisions: All three-word stream handles use void(context,i1 destroy); false cancels without reclamation, true destroys. Cold deferred contexts no-op on cancel. This covers cold-backed event joins without allocating adapters.

Join cancellation settles runtime, signals event inputs without freeing them; false returns. True joins pulling workers BEFORE destroying inputs and owning context. Cold inputs are not cancelled because their next cannot block externally.

Mouse Windows cancellation wakes consumer and interrupts current worker IO. Destroy retries CancelSynchronousIo across bounded per-wait timeout until worker exits; WAIT_FAILED traps rather than silently restoring/freeing. Linux cancellation signals eventfd, destroy joins worker before restoring/freeing.
Reader counters and post-decrement event signalling removed from CSharp; caller quiescence owns callback entry gap and all next accesses. SLG already has no counter.
SLG ownership drop and both entry terminal cleanup calls must pass i1 true. Native handle/dynamic trait/task completion callbacks remain their own one-argument protocols.

SLG cold-backed join return repacks the same callback: use the shared signature. Direct Range->defer annotated EventStream remains rejected by current CSharp; no new public conversion feature requested.
limitations: Deterministic native leaf OS/worker boundaries are stubbed; not actual terminal or all OS scheduler interleavings.
CSharp actual controls and12 lifecycle cases pass; final CSharp/SLG proof and full goal gates pending.
